questions.question: A cylinder whose height is eight times its radius is melted and cast into spherical balls each of half the radius of the cylinder. Find the number of spherical balls.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume is conserved ⇒ Number of spheres = Volume of cylinder ÷ Volume of one sphere

Cylinder: h = 8r ⇒ Volume = πr² × 8r = 8πr³

Sphere: radius = r/2 ⇒ Volume = (4/3)π(r/2)³ = (1/6)πr³

Number = 8πr³ ÷ (1/6)πr³ = 8 × 6 = 48

**∴ Answer = 48**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cylinder radius = r, height = 8r; Sphere radius = r/2

**Formula used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h; Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

 
• 
• r 8r r/2 

Cylinder volume = πr² × 8r = 8πr³

Sphere volume = (4/3)π(r/2)³ = (1/6)πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Number of spheres = Total volume ÷ Volume of one sphere

⇒ = 8πr³ ÷ (1/6)πr³

⇒ = 8 × 6

⇒ = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid is melted and recast, total volume remains constant.

Cylinder Volume

Volume = πr²h

Sphere Volume

Volume = (4/3)πr³

Scaling Rule

If radius changes by factor k, volume changes by k³.

questions.question: One pipe can fill a tank in 6 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 9 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take total work = LCM(6, 9) = 18 units

Filling pipe = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 units/min, Emptying pipe = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 units/min

Net work = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/min

Half tank work = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 units ⇒ Time = 9 ÷ 1 = 9 min

**∴ Answer = 9 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe = 6 min, Emptying pipe = 9 min

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 Person/Pipe
 Time (min)
 Total Work
 Efficiency
 
 
 
 

 Fill Pipe
 6
 18
 18 ÷ 6 = 3
 
 

 Empty Pipe
 9
 18 ÷ 9 = 2
 
 

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of (6, 9) = 18

⇒ Filling rate = 3 units/min, Emptying rate = 2 units/min

⇒ Net rate = 1 unit/min

⇒ Work for half tank = 9 units

⇒ Time = 9 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 9 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Assume total work as LCM of given times to simplify calculations and avoid fractions.

Net Efficiency

Net work = Filling rate − Emptying rate when pipes work together.

Work-Time Relation

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

Half Work Concept

Time for half work = (Half work) ÷ Net efficiency

questions.question: In a test, B got 50 marks while A got 75 marks, out of 110 maximum marks. What percentage of A’s marks was B’s marks? (Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required % = (B ÷ A) × 100

= (50 ÷ 75) × 100

= (2 ÷ 3) × 100

= 66.67%

**∴ Answer = 66.67%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A’s marks = 75, B’s marks = 50

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Required % = (50 ÷ 75) × 100

⇒ = 0.6666 × 100

⇒ = 66.666…%

⇒ ≈ 66.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Formula

Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100

Fraction to Percentage

To convert fraction into %, multiply by 100

Simplification Trick

Reduce fraction first: 50/75 = 2/3 for faster calculation

Rounding Rule

Round to two decimal places: 66.666… ≈ 66.67%

questions.question: A food outlet sells two types of meal combos. The first combo contains 2 sandwiches and 1 juice and costs ₹80. The second combo contains 1 sandwich and 2 juices and costs ₹70. What is the price of one sandwich?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let sandwich = S, juice = J

2S + J = 80 and S + 2J = 70

Multiply second: 2S + 4J = 140

Subtract: (2S + 4J) − (2S + J) = 140 − 80 ⇒ 3J = 60 ⇒ J = 20

Put in S + 2J = 70 ⇒ S + 40 = 70 ⇒ S = 30

**∴ Answer = ₹30**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

2 sandwiches + 1 juice = 80, 1 sandwich + 2 juices = 70

**Formula used:**

Linear equations method

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let sandwich = S, juice = J

⇒ 2S + J = 80 ...(1)

⇒ S + 2J = 70 ...(2)

⇒ From (2): S = 70 − 2J

⇒ Substitute in (1): 2(70 − 2J) + J = 80

⇒ 140 − 4J + J = 80

⇒ 140 − 3J = 80

⇒ 3J = 60 ⇒ J = 20

⇒ S = 70 − 2(20) = 30

**∴ The correct answer is ₹30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations

Two equations with two variables can be solved using substitution or elimination method.

Elimination Method

Make coefficients same and subtract to eliminate one variable.

Substitution Method

Express one variable in terms of another and substitute.

Quick Check

Put values back: 2×30+20=80 and 30+40=70 ✔

questions.question: In a race, an athlete covers a distance of 420 m in 140 sec in the first lap. He covers the second lap of the same distance in 70 sec. What is the average speed (in m/sec) of the athlete?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equal distances ⇒ Average speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y)

First speed = 420 ÷ 140 = 3 m/sec, Second speed = 420 ÷ 70 = 6 m/sec

Average speed = (2 × 3 × 6) ÷ (3 + 6)

= 36 ÷ 9 = 4 m/sec

**∴ Answer = 4 m/sec**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of each lap = 420 m; Time₁ = 140 sec; Time₂ = 70 sec

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 420 + 420 = 840 m

⇒ Total time = 140 + 70 = 210 sec

⇒ Average speed = 840 ÷ 210

⇒ = 4 m/sec

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General)

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Equal Distance Formula

If distances are equal: Avg speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y)

Unit Check

Speed = m/sec when distance in meters and time in seconds

Common Mistake

Do not take simple average of speeds unless time is equal

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3:4 and their HCF is 7. Their LCM is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers = 3x and 4x (since ratio is 3:4)

HCF = x = 7

Numbers = 21 and 28

LCM = (21 × 28) ÷ 7 = 84

**∴ Answer = 84**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio = 3 : 4, HCF = 7

**Formula used:**

Product of numbers = HCF × LCM

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let numbers be 3x and 4x

⇒ HCF = x = 7

⇒ Numbers = 21 and 28

⇒ Product = 21 × 28 = 588

⇒ LCM = 588 ÷ 7 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers: Product = HCF × LCM

Ratio Method

If ratio is a:b, numbers can be written as ax and bx

Key Insight

When ratio is given, HCF is the common multiplier

Quick Trick

LCM = (Product of ratio terms × HCF)

questions.question: A person is 5 years older than twice their sibling’s age. If the person is currently 27 years old, how old is the sibling?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let sibling = x

Given: 27 = 2x + 5

⇒ 2x = 22 ⇒ x = 11

Sibling’s age = 11 years

**∴ Answer = 11 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Person’s age = 27 years

**Formula used:**

Linear equation relation

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let sibling’s age = x

⇒ Person’s age = 2x + 5

⇒ 2x + 5 = 27

⇒ 2x = 27 − 5

⇒ 2x = 22

⇒ x = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation

An equation involving one variable can be solved by isolating the variable.

Age Problems

Translate words into equations carefully before solving.

Key Translation

Twice the age = 2x, 5 years older = +5

Verification

2×11 + 5 = 27 ✔

10% of CP = 1280

⇒ CP = 12800

⇒ SP₁ = 1.07x

⇒ SP₂ = 1.17x

⇒ Difference = 1.17x − 1.07x

⇒ 0.10x = 1280

questions.question: A room with a square base and height 10 ft occupies 25,000 ft³ volume. The room has cubicles of base area 25 ft² in four corners. The walls and ceiling of the area of the room which is not occupied by cubicles is to be painted. How much area is to be painted?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume = base area × height ⇒ Base = 25000 ÷ 10 = 2500 ft² ⇒ side = 50 ft

Wall area = perimeter × height = (4 × 50) × 10 = 2000 ft²

Cubicles: each side = 5 ⇒ blocked per wall = 5 + 5 = 10 ⇒ effective wall = 50 − 10 = 40

New wall area = 4 × 40 × 10 = 1600 ft²; Ceiling left = 2500 − (4 × 25) = 2400 ft²

Total area = 1600 + 2400 = 4000 ft²

**∴ Answer = 4000 ft²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume = 25000 ft³, Height = 10 ft, Cubicle base = 25 ft² each (4 cubicles)

**Formula used:**

Volume = side² × height; Wall area = perimeter × height

 50 ft 50 ft Room 

Base area = 25000 ÷ 10 = 2500 ft²

Side = √2500 = 50 ft

Each cubicle side = √25 = 5 ft

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total wall area = 4 × 50 × 10 = 2000 ft²

⇒ Blocked wall per side = 5 + 5 = 10 ft

⇒ Effective wall per side = 40 ft

⇒ Wall area to paint = 4 × 40 × 10 = 1600 ft²

⇒ Ceiling area = 2500 − (4 × 25) = 2400 ft²

⇒ Total painted area = 1600 + 2400 = 4000 ft²

**∴ The correct answer is 4000 ft².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Relation

Volume of cuboid = base area × height

Wall Area

Lateral surface area = perimeter × height

Square Room

Side = √(base area)

Area Deduction

Subtract cubicle occupied areas from total before painting

questions.question: A dealer marks his goods at 44% above the cost price and allows a discount of 75% on the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100

MP = 144 (since 44% above CP)

After 75% discount ⇒ SP = 25% of 144 = 36

Loss = 100 − 36 = 64%

**∴ Answer = 64% Loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price = 44% above CP, Discount = 75%

**Formula used:**

MP = CP × (1 + Markup/100), SP = MP × (1 − Discount/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = x

⇒ MP = 1.44x

⇒ SP = 1.44x × 0.25 = 0.36x

⇒ Loss = x − 0.36x = 0.64x

⇒ Loss% = (0.64x ÷ x) × 100

⇒ = 64%

**∴ The correct answer is 64% Loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup Concept

MP = CP × (1 + markup%)

Discount Concept

SP = MP × (1 − discount%)

Net Effect

Successive percentage changes multiply, not add

Quick Trick

Take CP = 100 to simplify percentage problems

questions.question: If 4⁽x ⁺ ¹⁾ = 64 × 8x find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all terms to base 2

4 = 2², 64 = 2⁶, 8 = 2³

2²⁽x⁺¹⁾ = 2⁶ × 2³x = 2⁶⁺³x

Equate powers ⇒ 2x + 2 = 6 + 3x ⇒ x = −4

**∴ Answer = −4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

4⁽x ⁺ ¹⁾ = 64 × 8x

**Formula used:**

am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ, (am)ⁿ = amⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ 4⁽x⁺¹⁾ = (2²)⁽x⁺¹⁾ = 2²x⁺²

⇒ 64 × 8x = 2⁶ × (2³)x = 2⁶⁺³x

⇒ 2²x⁺² = 2⁶⁺³x

⇒ 2x + 2 = 6 + 3x

⇒ 2 − 6 = 3x − 2x

⇒ −4 = x

**∴ The correct answer is −4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exponent Rule

am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

Power of Power

(am)ⁿ = amⁿ

Equal Bases

If bases are equal, equate exponents directly

Standard Bases

4 = 2², 8 = 2³, 64 = 2⁶

questions.question: ₹1,964 is divided among Ashish, Lalita and Pranav in such a way that if ₹50, ₹17 and ₹10 are deducted from their respective shares, they have money in the ratio 20:4:13. Find Lalita’s share.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let remaining shares be 20k : 4k : 13k

Original shares = (20k+50), (4k+17), (13k+10)

Total ⇒ 37k + 77 = 1964

⇒ 37k = 1887 ⇒ k = 51

Lalita’s share = 4k + 17 = 204 + 17 = 221

**∴ Answer = ₹221**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = 1964; After deduction ratio = 20 : 4 : 13

**Formula used:**

Ratio method with variable k

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let shares after deduction = 20k, 4k, 13k

⇒ Original shares = 20k + 50, 4k + 17, 13k + 10

⇒ Total = (20k + 50) + (4k + 17) + (13k + 10)

⇒ 37k + 77 = 1964

⇒ 37k = 1887

⇒ k = 51

⇒ Lalita’s share = 4k + 17 = 4×51 + 17 = 221

**∴ The correct answer is ₹221.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Concept

If quantities are in ratio a:b:c, they can be written as ak, bk, ck

Adjustment Method

Add back deducted amounts to get original values

Equation Formation

Sum of all shares equals total amount

Quick Tip

Always form equation after reversing deductions

questions.question: Mohan can complete a piece of work alone in 6 days by working 5 hours a day, and Rohan can do the same in 8 days. If they work together for 8 hours each day, how long will it take them to finish the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mohan: 6 days × 5 hr = 30 hr ⇒ rate = 1/30 per hr

Rohan: 8 days × 5 hr = 40 hr ⇒ rate = 1/40 per hr

Combined rate = 1/30 + 1/40 = (4 + 3)/120 = 7/120 per hr

Time = 120/7 hr ⇒ per day (8 hr) ⇒ (120/7) ÷ 8 = 2(1)/(7) days

**∴ Answer = 2(1)/(7) days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mohan: 6 days at 5 hr/day; Rohan: 8 days at 5 hr/day; Together: 8 hr/day

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

 
 

 Person
 Total Hours
 Total Work
 Efficiency
 
 
 
 

 Mohan
 30
 120
 120 ÷ 30 = 4
 
 

 Rohan
 40
 120 ÷ 40 = 3
 
 

 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mohan time = 30 hr, Rohan time = 40 hr

⇒ LCM = 120 units

⇒ Efficiency: Mohan = 4, Rohan = 3

⇒ Combined = 7 units/hr

⇒ Total time = 120 ÷ 7 hr

⇒ In days = (120 ÷ 7) ÷ 8 = 2(1)/(7) days

**∴ The correct answer is 2(1)/(7) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Conversion

Convert days into hours when working hours differ

LCM Method

Combined Work

Time Conversion

Convert total hours into days based on daily working hours

questions.question: Simplify: [(4x - 5y)² + 80xy​] ÷ [(4x + 5y)²]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

(4x − 5y)² = 16x² − 40xy + 25y²

Add 80xy ⇒ 16x² + 40xy + 25y²

This becomes (4x + 5y)²

**∴ Answer = 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

[(4x − 5y)² + 80xy] ÷ [(4x + 5y)²]

**Concept Used:**

Algebraic identities

**Calculation:**

⇒ [(4x − 5y)² + 80xy] ÷ [(4x + 5y)²]

⇒ [16x² − 40xy + 25y² + 80xy] ÷ [(4x + 5y)²]

⇒ [16x² + 40xy + 25y²] ÷ [(4x + 5y)²]

⇒ [(4x + 5y)²] ÷ [(4x + 5y)²]

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Order: Brackets → Orders → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction

Important Identity

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

Simplification Trick

Try converting numerator into denominator form

Cancellation

Same terms in numerator and denominator cancel out

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 40%, 15% and 45% in three successive months, but increases by 70% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take initial price = 100

After changes ⇒ 100 × 0.60 × 0.85 × 0.55 × 1.70

= 100 × 0.47685 = 47.685

Change = 47.685 − 100 = −52.315%

**∴ Answer = 52.32% decrease**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive changes: −40%, −15%, −45%, +70%

**Formula used:**

Net change = Product of multipliers

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let initial price = 100

⇒ After 1st: 100 × 0.60 = 60

⇒ After 2nd: 60 × 0.85 = 51

⇒ After 3rd: 51 × 0.55 = 28.05

⇒ After 4th: 28.05 × 1.70 = 47.685

⇒ Net change = 47.685 − 100 = −52.315

⇒ ≈ −52.32%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.32% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

Use multipliers: (1 ± p/100) for each change

Multipliers

Decrease ⇒ multiply by (1 − p/100), Increase ⇒ (1 + p/100)

Important Tip

Successive changes are multiplicative, not additive

Rounding Rule

Round final percentage to two decimal places

questions.question: The average age of 23 students of a class is 25 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 26 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total age of students = 23 × 25 = 575

New total (including teacher) = 24 × 26 = 624

Teacher’s age = 624 − 575 = 49

**∴ Answer = 49 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 23, Average age = 25; New average = 26 (including teacher)

**Formula used:**

Total = Average × Number

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total age of students = 23 × 25 = 575

⇒ Total age including teacher = 24 × 26 = 624

⇒ Teacher’s age = 624 − 575 = 49

**∴ The correct answer is 49 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = Total ÷ Number ⇒ Total = Average × Number

Combined Average

When a new value is added, recompute total using new average

Quick Trick

Extra total = Difference in average × new number

Application

Teacher’s age = increase in total after inclusion

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 19.8, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula to find the answer.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use empirical formula: Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

Given: Mode − Mean = 19.8

⇒ (3Median − 2Mean) − Mean = 19.8 ⇒ 3Median − 3Mean = 19.8

⇒ Median − Mean = 6.6 ⇒ Mode − Median = 19.8 − 6.6 = 13.2

**∴ Answer = 13.2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode − Mean = 19.8

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mode − Mean = (3Median − 2Mean) − Mean

⇒ = 3Median − 3Mean

⇒ 3(Median − Mean) = 19.8

⇒ Median − Mean = 6.6

⇒ Mode − Median = (Mode − Mean) − (Median − Mean)

⇒ = 19.8 − 6.6

⇒ = 13.2

**∴ The correct answer is 13.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

Derived Relation

Mode − Mean = 3(Median − Mean)

Key Trick

First find Median − Mean, then subtract from given difference

Usage

Applicable for moderately skewed distributions

questions.question: Walking at (3)/(5) of his normal speed from his home, Vishal is 24 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 3/5 ⇒ Time ratio = 5/3

Extra time = (5/3 − 1) = 2/3 of usual time

⇒ (2/3) of usual time = 24 min

⇒ Usual time = 24 × (3/2) = 36 min

**∴ Answer = 36 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = (3/5) of normal speed; Extra time = 24 min

**Formula used:**

Time ∝ 1/Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let usual time = t

⇒ New time = t × (5/3)

⇒ Extra time = t × (5/3 − 1)

⇒ t × (2/3) = 24

⇒ t = 24 × (3/2)

⇒ t = 36 min

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

Time ∝ 1/Speed for fixed distance

Ratio Trick

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a

Extra Time

Extra time = New time − Original time

Quick Method

Use fractional difference directly to find original time

⇒ X² = 625

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following four schemes:

A) Two successive discounts of 32% and 40%

B) Buy 1, get 5 free

C) A single discount of 48%

D) Two successive discounts of 8% and 33%

Which scheme is best for the shopkeeper?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare effective discounts

A: 32% & 40% ⇒ Net = 1 − (0.68 × 0.60) = 59.2%

B: Buy 1 get 5 free ⇒ Pay 1 for 6 ⇒ Discount = 5/6 ≈ 83.33%

C: 48% discount

D: 8% & 33% ⇒ Net = 1 − (0.92 × 0.67) = 38.36%

Least discount = best for shopkeeper ⇒ D

**∴ Answer = Option D**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four discount schemes

**Formula used:**

Successive discount = 1 − (1 − a)(1 − b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ A: 1 − (0.68 × 0.60) = 1 − 0.408 = 59.2%

⇒ B: Buy 1 get 5 free ⇒ Discount = 5/6 × 100 ≈ 83.33%

⇒ C: 48%

⇒ D: 1 − (0.92 × 0.67) = 1 − 0.6164 = 38.36%

⇒ Minimum discount = 38.36%

**∴ The correct answer is Option D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

Net discount = 1 − (1 − a)(1 − b)

B1G Free Concept

Effective discount = Free items ÷ Total items

Shopkeeper Benefit

Lower discount ⇒ higher profit

Quick Tip

Always convert all schemes into effective discount for comparison

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 32° and ∠B = 58°. The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O. What is the measure of ∠DOC?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use formula: angle between bisectors of two adjacent angles = 180 − (sum of the other two angles)/2

⇒ A + D = 360 − (B + C)

Required ∠BOC = 180 − (A + D)/2 = (B + C)/2

⇒ B = 58°, A = 32° ⇒ C + D = 270°

Hence ∠BOC = (B + C)/2 ⇒ = (58 + C)/2 but using symmetry ⇒ = (A + B)/2

= (32 + 58)/2 = 45°

**∴ Answer = 45°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠A = 32°, ∠B = 58°; Bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at O

**Formula used:**

Sum of angles of quadrilateral = 360°

 
 
• 
• A B C D O 

∠C + ∠D = 360 − (32 + 58) = 270°

**Calculation:**

⇒ Angle between bisectors of B and C = 180 − (A + D)/2

⇒ A + D = 360 − (B + C)

⇒ ∠BOC = 180 − (360 − (B + C))/2

⇒ = (B + C)/2

⇒ = (32 + 58)/2

⇒ = 45°

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quadrilateral Angle Sum

A + B + C + D = 360°

Angle Bisector Result

Angle between bisectors of adjacent angles = half of sum of opposite angles

Key Insight

Result depends only on given angles A and B

Shortcut Idea

Final angle = (A + B)/2
